01 / Research spotlight

Can a more diverse calibration set make conformal prediction more useful?

Under distribution shift, annotated calibration examples are expensive. This research project studies whether a k-determinantal point process (k-DPP) can select a small, diverse target-domain calibration set that produces informative prediction sets without sacrificing honest coverage.

01Represent

Freeze a JEPA visual encoder and train a linear classifier on the source domain.

02Select

Compare k-DPP sampling with uniform selection at the same annotation budget.

03Test

Measure coverage, prediction-set size and stability on held-out target data.

The central challenge

Diversity-based selection changes the sampling scheme, so standard split-conformal exchangeability arguments cannot simply be reused. Whether coverage can be preserved—and under which conditions—is the question being investigated.

02 / Computer vision

Fine-grained visual retrieval

An end-to-end system that identifies the exact trading-card instance in a photograph, including near-identical variants distinguished by tiny visual details. The pipeline combines detection, geometric rectification, DINOv3 embeddings and similarity search.

03 / Probabilistic modelling

Forecasting Brest temperatures and future extremes

A stochastic modelling project using Brest air-temperature records from 1940–2025. The goal is not one deterministic forecast, but an ensemble of plausible future daily trajectories conditioned on CO₂ scenarios—and a careful estimate of rare heat and cold events.

The modelling framework combines seasonal decomposition with a CO₂-conditioned diffusion model of daily temperature residuals. Temporal backtests and an extreme-value baseline will be used to assess rare heat and cold events.

PyTorchDiffusionTime seriesExtreme values
04 / Medical AI · Inserm LaTIM

Benchmarking local vision-language models for oncology imaging

With Inserm LaTIM in Brest, this project will compare open-source VLMs run locally as evaluators of AI-generated medical images. The planned benchmark asks whether they can assess anatomical and tumour fidelity, and how their judgments compare with conventional metrics and clinical experts.
